ranking.note: Raised to P1: shipped release binaries silently lose BTI/CET hardening markers, a security defect in the released artifact comparable to #35765's build-corruption risk.
Moved up: it is the only PR here fixing an installed binary that simply does not run for users of common distributions (issue #35785), which outranks portability and coverage work.
Raised to P2 and moved up: removal of a recurring dependency burden across depends, Guix, CMake and tidy/IWYU tooling is the same class of durable value as the compiler-baseline PRs.
Raised to P2: it is the stated prerequisite for multiprocess on Windows (#28722), i.e. enables a supported platform for a category-defining project, not mere resource-file churn.
Moved up: it fixes an actual Guix configure failure for emulated cross-system builds, ranking above convenience and warning-flag work in this band.
Moved up: fixes a real functional-test failure on a platform plus adds per-PR CI enforcement, ahead of purely additive tooling.
Moved down slightly below concrete breakage fixes: it is structural CMake work with no current build failure attached.
Moved up: signing-certificate expiry directly threatens release engineering timelines, which this category weighs above developer convenience.
Moved down: removing privileged CI containers is valuable but trades away eBPF-path coverage, placing it below the unambiguous breakage fixes above.
Moved down marginally: a preventive hermeticity check, below fixes for failures already observed.
Moved down: speculative maintainer-convenience tooling with no failure it currently fixes.
Moved down: packaging convenience, below CI-reliability and build-failure items in the same band.
Moved up: enabling invariant checking in existing CI jobs can surface real container-corruption bugs, more than cosmetic link/doc hygiene below it.
Moved down: affects only non-default builds against an external libmultiprocess, the narrowest fix in this band.
Lowered to P4 for consistency with the other diagnostic-hygiene flag PRs (#36268, #36704): it prevents spurious warnings rather than catching a bug class.

inconsistencies: Chain: #36082 (Guix builds in CI) is described as the coverage needed to safely land #25573 (static-pie release binaries); review #36082 first.
Chain: #36042 (g++ 13 minimum) is the concrete step underneath #36033 (require C++23 RFC). Decide #36042 first; #36033 is the policy decision it feeds.
Chain: #36781 is explicitly based on #36743; #36743 must be settled first, and #36781 adds no value if #36743 is rejected.

Warning-flag family (#36167, #36743, #35911, #36268, #36704, #36781) all touch large overlapping swathes of the tree; they will conflict with each other. #36167 has the strongest justification (catches dead code and real logic bugs, per #36137) and should be reviewed first of the group.

libmultiprocess build cluster: #35068 (depends CMake discovery, breaks native_libmultiprocess), #36556 (capnp TSan false races), #35454 (external libmultiprocess example targets) and #32387 (Windows IPC) all gate the same subsystem; #35068 and #36556 unblock builds/CI and should precede the narrower #35454.
Release-branch pair: #36589 and #36727 both backport to 32.x; they will interact and are best reviewed together, #36589 first since it restores the ability to produce release binaries at all.

Overlapping goal: #36147 (native BSD CI jobs) and #36587 (NetBSD IPC test fix plus FD-limit enforcement in macOS CI) both target BSD/FD-limit regressions escaping to nightly runs; #36147 is the broader mechanism and sets the context for #36587.
#36593 depends on #36592, which is not present in this list; its reviewability depends on that prerequisite landing.
#19460 depends on #10102 and #29409 and unblocks #19461; it is multiprocess feature plumbing that only incidentally lands in this category.
result.notes: The category splits cleanly: two PRs threaten the integrity of the artifacts actually shipped (#35765 wrong source tree, #36534 missing hardening markers) and sit alone at P1; a band of release-infrastructure and supported-platform work follows at P2; the large P3 block is mostly CI coverage and build-failure fixes; and a tail of compiler-warning and documentation hygiene PRs sits at P4. I kept the six warning-flag PRs split between P3 and P4 on whether the flag catches a real defect class or only tidies diagnostics, rather than banding them all together.
